summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi around 1976–1982. He served as a lecturer at Kindai University.

Atsushi Uno studied at Kyoto University and Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti and other scholars. A scholar of Indology and philosophy, he held posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima, and Kindai universities.

Atsuuji Ashikaga worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Doshisha University and under Ryosaburo Sakaki, later serving as a professor at Kyoto University around 1950–1965.

Atsuyoshi Sakakura, a scholar of Japanology and linguistics, studied at Kyoto University from around 1938 to 1941. He later held academic posts at Kyoto University (circa 1963–1981) and Konan Women's University (circa 1981–1993).

August Fick was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He later held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1869–1887) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).
August Friedrich Pott was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Göttingen and Berlin. In 1833, he was appointed Professor of General Linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg.

August Johan Bernet Kempers was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at Leiden University. He directed the Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and the University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Kiel, Leipzig under Georg Curtius, and Jena under August Schleicher. He held posts at Jena and Göttingen before serving as a professor at Leipzig University from around 1870 to 1916.

August Schleicher studied linguistics and Indology at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others. He held academic posts at Bonn, Charles University as Professor of Philology, and the University of Jena.

August Wilhelm Schlegel studied at Göttingen, Paris, and under Franz Bopp, working in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1796–1801) and as a professor at the University of Bonn from 1818.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle was an Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics scholar. He served as director at Aliah University around 1881–1899 and as secretary of the Asiatic Society in 1891.

Awadh Kishore Narain studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS University of London. Working in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1954–1971) and as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1971–1988).
Axel Michaels is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1992–1996) and Heidelberg University (~1996–2014).

B. Alan Wallace works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, having earned a PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt. He held posts at UC Santa Barbara and heads the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.

B. N. Mukherjee was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta from around 1951 to 1955. He later held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from around 1975 to 1997.

B. R. Ambedkar studied at Elphinstone College, Columbia University, LSE, University of Bonn, and University of London, working in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as professor of economics at Sydenham College (~1918–1920).

Baatr U. Kitinov earned a Ph.D. in World History at Moscow State University. Specializing in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Tibetology, he became an Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia around 2004.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1935–1965), became Government Epigraphist for India in 1950, and was Professor of Ancient Indian Culture and Archaeology at Panjab University in 1965.

Baiei Henmi, who worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology, studied at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1915 to 1918. He later held a post at Tama Art University from around 1953 to 1972.

Baihui Wu was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1952), became Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University around 1952, and worked at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of Philosophy around 1978.
